transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Rivera, thank you for coming in today. I asked to meet with you because I need to discuss a serious mistake that was made in your son's medical record.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A mistake?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes. When your son was due for his developmental screening, the referral was marked as completed in our computer system. This happened even though the appointment didn't actually take place. Because it was marked as done, the system didn't alert us to follow up, and he didn't receive the screening he needed during that critical window.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I remember we missed one date. I thought it was okay because it was just one time.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm sorry for any confusion this caused. We were just really busy in the clinic during that period, but the referral should have been tracked better.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is that why he is not talking yet?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The delay in screening means we missed the chance for early intervention. At this stage, the developmental gaps are much harder to close. It's likely he will have permanent challenges with his speech and cognitive growth.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't understand. Permanent? Like he will never be normal?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It means the prognostic outlook is significantly altered. He will likely need lifelong support services.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I... I can't believe this. My son.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. But we have to focus on what we can do now, so let's move to the next steps.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am worried. I don't have papers. Will this... if I start these services, will the government find us?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. Now, regarding the plan, I have already coordinated with the early intervention team. I have scheduled a comprehensive neuro-psychological evaluation for this coming Tuesday at 10:00 AM. I have also contacted a social worker who specializes in undocumented families to ensure your privacy is protected.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Tuesday. I have to work.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I've already arranged for a telehealth option if you can't make it in, but in-person is better. I want you to call my office by tomorrow at 4:00 PM to confirm which one you prefer. Also, I am enrolling your son in a daily speech therapy program starting next Monday. I will provide you with a written schedule and a list of the specific therapists.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What happens if he doesn't get better?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We can't say for sure, but we are implementing a high-intensity protocol. To make sure this never happens again, our department is changing how we track referrals. We are moving to a double-verification system where two different nurses must sign off on a completed screening. I've also flagged your son's chart for a monthly manual review by the attending physician for the next year.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel like I failed him.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. Now, let's go over the paperwork for the social worker.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just... I can't stop thinking about what you said. About him never being the same.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know it's a lot, but I really have to get to my next appointment in a few minutes, so let's just make sure we're clear on the Tuesday date. Do you have a pen to write this down?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Great. Tuesday at 10:00 AM. Then Monday for speech. You call me by 4:00 PM tomorrow. Does that sound like a clear plan to you?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes. I think so.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Good. I'll have my assistant give you the folder with the therapists' names on your way out.

H.justification: The resident uses rushing language multiple times, specifically stating they 'have to get to my next appointment in a few minutes' and 'let's just make sure we're clear'.

E.justification: The error is named explicitly in the first turn using lay language, and the resident checks for comprehension at the end ('Does that sound like a clear plan to you?').

A.justification: While the resident says 'I'm sorry', the apology is immediately diluted by an excuse regarding being 'really busy in the clinic'.

R.justification: The resident relies exclusively on generic validation ('I understand') and does not name specific emotions or engage with the patient's emotional bids.

T.justification: The resident provides specific next steps with timelines (Tuesday 10am, Monday speech), a named patient role (call by 4pm tomorrow), and a detailed prevention plan (double-verification system).
